      • testFlushQueueRequst

        public void testFlushQueueRequst()
        Flush queue request should release all messages (RO and TSO) currently held in the message queue up until the specified time. It gives no regard to the LBTS, so messages can be delivered out-of-order and on completion a time advance can be granted to a time where the RTI can't guarantee that events in the past aren't possible.

        This test will send events with timestamps beyond what would normally be delivered from the defaultFederate to the secondFederate and will then flush the queue of the second federate and expect to see those messages come in.

      • testFlushQueueRequestAdvancesConstrainedFederate

        public void testFlushQueueRequestAdvancesConstrainedFederate()
        The flushQueueRequest call instructs the LRC to drain all current messages (RO and TSO) up to a specific time, even if this means violating ordering. It then issues a time advance for the federate to either the cutoff time or the timestamp of the next TSO even, whichever is smaller. This is done without any guarantee that messages with a lower timestamp might show up later on (hence the reason this is referred to as optimistic time management).

        As such, if this service is working properly, a constrained federate should be able to advance itself beyond the federation LBTS. This method asserts that this is infact true.
